To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensity volumes were strongly correlated with total white matter hyperintense volume in a sample of 55 elderly subjects.

periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden were highly correlated with each another and with the total burden, and that the spatial distribution of WMH did not support a distinction between periventricual WMH and deep WMH.

periventricular WM hyperintensities and deep WM hyperintensites are highly correlated with total white matter hyperintensity volume and that spatial analysis failed to reveal distinct populations of periventricular and deep WM hyperinensities.

the relationships between periventricualr white matter hyperintensity (PVWMH), deep white matter hyperintesity (DWMH), and total white matter hyperintenisty (WMH) burden.
the relationships among periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensity (WMH) and total WMH volume.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the categorical distinctions between perivenricular and deep white matter hyperintensity are likely arbitrary and that the relationships between causal factors and behavioral consequences for these two types of hyperintensity are more likely to reflect the relationships between total white matter hyperintesity volume and the factors or behaviors of interest.
